fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Master switch. When off, every gateway call raises instead of contacting Intacct.

fields.label: Post Stock Movements to Intacct
fields.description: OFF by default. While off, stock movements are recorded in ERPNext only. Turn it on when the site is ready to post — from then on, a movement Intacct rejects will not submit in ERPNext either.

fields.label: Company ID
fields.description: One Intacct company per ERPNext site.

fields.label: Entity ID (locationid)
fields.description: Manufacturing transaction definitions are set to 'Entity only'. Without this the login is rejected with BL01001973.

fields.label: Transactions
fields.description: Which Intacct definition each Fuse process posts to. Every company names these differently — Leadertread's goods receipt is "Goods received voucher"; another company calls the same thing something else — so nothing here is defaulted from another client. The list is what THIS company has, read from Intacct; run fuse_core.transactions.sync_transaction_definitions to refresh it. A process with nothing mapped refuses to post rather than guessing.

fields.label: Active Modules
fields.description: Which parts of Fuse appear on the Fuse Home page. Switching one off removes its tile and nothing else — the screens behind it still work for anyone who reaches them another way. This is a launcher preference, not a permission.

fields.label: Query Page Size
fields.description: Intacct guidance is to keep queries UNDER about 1000 records, so the default sits below the ceiling rather than on it. More pages costs time, not concurrency — and time is cheap here.

fields.label: Max Attempts
fields.description: Transient failures only (timeout, empty response, 5xx, 429). A genuine rejection is never retried.

fields.label: Last Sync Result
fields.description: Outcome of the most recent background sync. A full sync cannot fit in a web request, so it runs on the long queue and reports here.

fields.label: Support Email
fields.description: Where a support ticket raised on this site is sent. Defaults to Syncflo. A partner supporting their own clients points it at their own desk, and nothing else changes.

fields.label: Discretionary Tickets Need Approval
fields.description:
On: a request for a change, an idea, training or a new user waits for someone holding the Fuse Support Approver role before it is sent. Faults never wait - something broken goes straight through, because an approver on leave must not be able to sit on a system that is down.

If nobody holds the role, the ticket is sent anyway and says so on the record. A gate nobody can open is not a control, it is a ticket that vanishes.
